convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load an external custom indicator 'MALR' with 5 parameters. The entry logic depends on buffers 3 and 4 of this custom indicator (high_extr/low_extr channels), which cannot be auto-converted without reimplementing the MALR indicator in Python. Additionally, the EA has complex position management (averaging, position overturn/martingale) that requires careful manual conversion.

derived_values.name: high_extr
derived_values.formula: CopyBuffer(handle_MALR, buffer_index=3, shift=1, count=2) - upper channel extremum from MALR custom indicator
derived_values.used_by: entry rule - short signal when close crosses above high_extr

derived_values.name: low_extr
derived_values.formula: CopyBuffer(handle_MALR, buffer_index=4, shift=1, count=2) - lower channel extremum from MALR custom indicator
derived_values.used_by: entry rule - long signal when close crosses below low_extr

derived_values.name: propn
derived_values.formula: IF position_type==BUY: prev_open - ASK; IF position_type==SELL: BID - prev_open (floating loss in price units)
derived_values.used_by: averaging entry logic - triggers averaging trade when loss exceeds threshold

params.note: sl input parameter in points; for 5-digit broker this is 255 pips
tp input parameter in points; for 5-digit broker this is 257.8 pips
Trail activates when price moves profit*points beyond open price (50 points profit). Then trails by trail*points (200 points).

other_exits: Position overturn: on opposite signal, existing position is closed and reversed with volume multiplied by koff_multiplication (default 2.0x)
Averaging: when floating loss exceeds loss_forAveraging*point (500 points), an additional same-direction trade is opened with the same volume as the last non-overturn entry (prev_avlot)

params.scaling_formula: Lot * AccountEquity / Max_drawdown when use_increase=true and no existing position
params.averaging_lot: same as last main entry lot (prev_avlot)

position_sizing.conditional_logic: if use_increase=true and vol==0 and no open position: lot = Lot * equity / Max_drawdown; if mode==3 (overturn): lot = prev_lot * koff_multiplication; if mode==2 (averaging): lot = prev_avlot; otherwise: lot = Lot (0.1)

custom_logic_notes: The core signal logic depends on the MALR custom indicator's buffers 3 (high_extr - upper channel) and 4 (low_extr - lower channel). Entry signal: previous bar close was below low_extr AND current bar close is above low_extr => BUY (crossover up through lower channel). Previous bar close was above high_extr AND current bar close is below high_extr => SELL (crossover down through upper channel). The condition high_extr[0]<=close[0] && high_extr[1]>=close[1] means: bar[1] close was at or above high_extr[1], and bar[0] close is at or below high_extr[0] - i.e., close crossed below the high channel. Three trade modes: mode=1 (Main), mode=2 (Averaging), mode=3 (Overturn/reversal with multiplied lot). Position overturn closes existing position and opens reverse with 2x volume. Averaging opens additional same-direction position when floating loss exceeds threshold. The SL/TP is set after order fill via modify loop (up to N_modify_sltp=7 retries with 1s sleep). The MALR indicator source code is required for Python backtest conversion.
external_dependencies: MALR custom indicator (iCustom call with params: MAPeriod=120, MAShift=0, AppliedPrice=PRICE_CLOSE, ChannelReversal=1.1, ChannelBreakout=1.1) - requires the .mq5 or .ex5 indicator file to understand buffer 3 and buffer 4 logic
backtest_data_needs: Any symbol with 5-digit pricing, H1 or default timeframe, 730 days
python_conversion_notes: The MALR custom indicator must be reverse-engineered or obtained separately. It appears to be a Moving Average Linear Regression channel indicator with buffers: likely buffer 0=MA line, buffer 1=upper reversal channel, buffer 2=lower reversal channel or breakout, buffer 3=high extremum, buffer 4=low extremum. Without the MALR source, the channel calculation logic is unknown. The entry crossover logic (close crossing above low_extr for buy, close crossing below high_extr for sell) can be reimplemented if MALR math is understood. Position management has three modes that interact: (1) Main entry on signal, (2) Averaging on deep loss, (3) Overturn on reversal signal. These must be modeled carefully as they affect net position and lot sizing. The trailing stop uses profit-based activation (price must move 50 points into profit before trail engages, then trails by 200 points). SL/TP retry loop with Sleep(1000) should be simplified for backtest - just set SL/TP at order time.
